messages.content: I want to find a song now, and I know that there are some really good songs in the album called We Are Not Your Kind, I enjoy Rock-and-roll songs which are from the '19.

function.name: Music_3_PlayMedia
function.description: Initiates playback of a specified music track on a designated device. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

track.description: The title of the track to be played.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the track.

device.description: The name or location of the device where the music will be played.

album.description: The name of the album that the track is from, if applicable.

function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Finds songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on the artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the song. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

album.description: The name of the album that the song is part of. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

genre.description: The genre of the music. Use 'dontcare' to indicate no specific preference.

year.description: The year of the song's initial release. Format should be a four-digit number, e.g., '2001'. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find a song. They mention an album called "We Are Not Your Kind". That seems like it's actually an album? Wait, "We Are Not Your Kind" might be an album by... Actually, "We Are Not Your Kind" sounds like maybe a band? Let's parse.

User says: "there are some really good songs in the album called We Are Not Your Kind." So they think there's an album named "We Are Not Your Kind".

They also say: "I enjoy Rock-and-roll songs which are from the '19."

So we need to search for songs matching criteria:

Artist: unknown (maybe don't care)
Album: "We Are Not Your Kind"? But that's likely not correct; but let's treat as album filter.

Genre: Rock? They said rock-and-roll. In our tool options, genres include "Rock". Good.

Year: "2019"? Our tool only supports years up to 2019 inclusive? It lists 2010-2019 plus dontcare. Yes includes 2019. Great.

Thus call Music_3_LookupMusic with:
artist="dontcare",
album="We Are Not Your Kind",
genre="Rock",
year="2019"

But note that the album may not exist. However we can still query. We'll use the function.
